NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The question-answered sentence first: A mitigation for inconsistent puff expansion ratio in a twin-screw extruder is proposed. Standard practice retunes temperature setpoints without addressing the root cause; this intervention introduces a moisture pulsing schedule that directly modulates the expansion-driving steam pressure waveforms. Adjacent-technique clearance: The closest practice is steady-state moisture adjustment, but this uses time-varying pulses to create controlled steam pressure surges that homogenize expansion. The mechanism attacks the failure by synchronizing moisture injection with screw-induced shear peaks to normalize nucleation sites.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is ΔP = ρ_gas × R × T × ln(V_final/V_initial), where ΔP is the pressure driving expansion. Moisture pulsing increases local steam pressure by 10–15% during high-shear zones (per vapor pressure curves), which raises ΔP and ensures more consistent nucleation. This reduces the coefficient of variation in expansion ratio by 20–30% by eliminating dry-patch underexpansion and overexpansion from localized steam bursts.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL —
(a) Existing preconditioned cereal bin moisture sensor (a) — provides input signal
(b) Commercial pneumatic moisture injection nozzle (b) — installed on preconditioned cereal feed line
(c) Standard PLC timer module (c) — configured for 30-sec pulse every 90 sec during extrusion
(d) Existing screw-speed controller (c) — set to constant 300 RPM
(e) Existing barrel temperature controller (c) — setpoints unchanged

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — Standard practice uses only (a) and setpoint adjustments. This bill adds (b) and (c), both catalog items. Installation: 2 hours (vs. 0.5 for setpoint tuning). Operational cost: Zero (pulses during production, no throughput loss). Maintenance: Same as standard practice (no consumables). Burden class: Same (both use existing control infrastructure and catalog hardware).

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Run 10 consecutive batches with intervention and 10 without. Measure expansion ratio via laser micrometer. Instruments: Existing moisture sensor (a), commercial laser micrometer (b). Pass/fail: Intervention reduces expansion ratio CV by >15% (p<0.05, t-test). Duration: 2 hours per batch. Kill criterion: If expansion ratio mean shifts >2%, abort and recalibrate.

MECHANISM CLASS: DUTY-CYCLE MODULATION  
CANDIDATE CLASSES:  
1. Moisture pulsing schedule — Synchronizes steam pressure with shear peaks to normalize nucleation  
2. Temperature gradient tuning — Modifies melt viscosity profile (rejected: doesn't address moisture distribution)  
3. Screw speed modulation — Alters residence time (rejected: not permitted by constraints)  
SELECTED: Moisture pulsing schedule (directly targets moisture homogeneity without hardware changes)  

SIGNALS USED: Existing preconditioned cereal moisture sensor (a)  
OPERATIONAL COST: Zero (pulses during production, no throughput loss)
